propositions: When an ephemeral runner's final push is rejected after the Jira rebar-id label is written but before local CREATE event and binding are durably published, the local state is lost while the label persists, creating a permanently stuck unbound_jira drift.
The binding_walk L10 guard currently stands down on any presence of a rebar-id label, preventing adoption replay even when the label is the sole residue of a lost partial commit.
Recovery must be keyed on the deterministic inbound local id (_jira_key_to_local_id) to ensure replayed adopts converge idempotently on the same binding and label without creating duplicates.

The fix conditionally relaxes the L10 stand-down only when: marker equals deterministic inbound id AND binding store has no entry AND local ticket does not exist — exactly the lost-adopt residue case.

Foreign, multi-marker, or already-stored keys retain unconditional stand-down; retired keys still route to SKIP_RETIRED; bridge_fsck remains untouched and continues alerting until binding is restored.
RED test confirms pre-fix walk stands down with adopted==[] on marked-but-unstored keys; post-fix replay machinery re-materializes the binding under the same deterministic id with no duplicate label.
